summary.en: A cleft sentence splits one idea into two parts to put the important information in focus. There are two main patterns. **It + be + focus + that / who…** points at one element: _It was the noise **that** kept me awake._ **What / All / The reason… + be + focus** builds up to the key information: _**What** I need is a holiday._ Both sound natural in speech and give your writing a more controlled, persuasive tone, which helps in Speaking part 4 and in the formal email of Writing part 4.
summary.es: Se divide la frase en dos partes para destacar lo importante, como en «fue el ruido lo que me despertó» o «lo que necesito es descansar». En inglés el verbo ser (be) siempre está en medio y no se repite el sujeto.

form: **It is / was** + focus + **that / who** + rest of the sentence (_who_ only for people)
**What** + subject + verb + **be** + focus (_What I need is…_, _What surprised me was…_)
**All** + subject + verb + **be** + focus (_All I want is…_)
**The reason (why)** + subject + verb + **be that**… (_The reason I called is that…_)
**The place where / The person who / The thing that** + clause + **be** + focus
**It was not until** + time + **that** + clause (_It wasn't until midnight that we arrived._)

uses.text: **Correcting or contrasting**: _It wasn't the price that put me off, it was the service._
**Putting new information last, where it has most impact**: _What worries me is how little time we have left._
**Stressing a time or place**: _It was in the evenings that she did her best work._
**Explaining reasons clearly in a formal email**: _The reason I am writing is that my order has not arrived._

mistakes.wrong: It was my sister which told me the news.
mistakes.right: It was my sister who told me the news.

why.en: When the focus is a person, use who (or that), never which.
why.es: Si el foco es una persona, who (o that), nunca which.

mistakes.wrong: It is the noise what bothers me.
mistakes.right: It is the noise that bothers me. / What bothers me is the noise.

why.en: What cannot follow a focused noun; use that, or build the what-pattern.
why.es: «Lo que» después de un nombre se dice that; what solo abre la frase.

mistakes.wrong: The reason why I left is because the pay was low.
mistakes.right: The reason I left is that the pay was low.

why.en: The reason already means because, so use that, not because.
why.es: The reason ya significa «porque»: no añadas because.

examples.en: It was the noise, not the heat, that kept me awake.
It is my manager who makes the final decision, not the board.
examples.es: Es mi jefe quien toma la decisión final, no la junta.

examples.en: What I need right now is a long holiday.
All I want is a quiet evening at home.
examples.es: Lo único que quiero es una tarde tranquila en casa.

examples.en: What surprised me most was how quickly she adapted.
The reason I am writing is that my order has not arrived.
It wasn't until I read the contract that I noticed the error.
What she did was apologise in front of the whole team.
The place where we first met has since been knocked down.
It was in the evenings that he got most of his work done.
What I'd really like is a sandwich and ten minutes' peace.
examples.es: Lo que de verdad me apetece es un bocadillo y diez minutos de paz.

practice.prompt: It was in the library ___ I lost my keys.

explanation.en: An it-cleft with a place as the focus is completed with that.

practice.prompt: ___ I need right now is a strong coffee.

explanation.en: The what-pattern opens with what and continues with be.

practice.prompt: The reason ___ I left the job was the low salary.

explanation.en: The reason (why) + clause + be + focus. Because and what do not fit here.

practice.prompt: All I want ___ a decent night's sleep.

explanation.en: All I want is + one thing: the verb be agrees with the singular complement.

practice.prompt: It wasn't until the end of the film ___ I realised who the thief was.

explanation.en: It wasn't until + time + that + clause.
